info.name: GenesisDB 2
info.description:
Requests for every route of the GenesisDB HTTP API, in a working order.

Set the collection variables `baseUrl` and `adminToken` (the value of `GENESISDB_AUTH_TOKEN`). Optional `readToken` and `writeToken` match `GENESISDB_READ_TOKEN` and `GENESISDB_WRITE_TOKEN`.

Run the folders top to bottom with the collection runner for a complete smoke test: `1 Health` needs no token, `2 Commit` writes sample data and stores event IDs in variables, the later folders read, query, audit, back up and erase it. `9 Authorization` expects 401/403 and only works when read and write tokens are configured.

List routes answer NDJSON (`application/x-ndjson`): one JSON object per line, each followed by an empty line. The test scripts parse that form. Single-object responses (status, 412 body, rebuild) are plain JSON.

Docs: docs/http-api.md and docs/gdbql.md in the repository.

variable.description: set by 7 Backup, used by Restore
any value that is not a configured token, used by 9 Authorization

request.description: Liveness. Answers the text `Pong`.
Liveness. Answers the text `Pong`.
Same as /ping.
Engine version and channel, host, event counts, storage format and readiness. Requires a token.

item.name: 2 Commit
item.description: Writes sample data. Later folders depend on the variables set here.

request.description: A subject with one segment (`/customer`) gets a generated ID appended. The response holds the stored events with ID, time, hashes. The customer subject and first event ID are saved in variables.
Several events in one atomic batch. The precondition `isSubjectExisting` must hold for the customer committed before. All events are published together or not at all.

`options.storeDataAsReference` stores the payload outside the immutable event, so `POST /erase` can remove it later without breaking the hash chain. Reads resolve the payload transparently, the API never exposes the reference key. `isSubjectNew` fails with 412 on the second run, which is expected.
`isQueryResultTrue` runs a GDBQL query under the writer lock and commits only if the result is true.
Expected to fail: `/order/1` exists already. Nothing is written.
Expected to fail: subject must start with `/`.

item.name: 3 Fetch
item.description: Reads a subject and its descendants in commit order.

request.description: Returns the customer event and the address change below it.
Bounds are event IDs. Everything from the first committed event up to the last event of the batch.

exec: pm.test("five events between the bounds", () => pm.expect(ndjson()).to.have.lengthOf(5));

request.description: Only the newest event of that type below the subject.

item.name: Fetch (legacy header x-disable-ndjson for a JSON array)

header.description: 1.x compatibility: answer one JSON array instead of NDJSON

request.description: Only for 1.x clients that cannot read NDJSON. With this header the list is one JSON array. Every other request in this collection uses the NDJSON default.

exec: pm.test("content type is JSON with the legacy header", () => pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get("Content-Type")).to.include("application/json"));

request.description: API v1 route of GenesisDB 1.x, answers like its API v2 successor plus `Deprecation` and `Link` headers.

item.name: 4 Query (GDBQL)
item.description: See docs/gdbql.md. Results are NDJSON rows, a single aggregate is a single value.

request.description: `UNDER` matches direct children of `/order`.
Typed comparison: `>= 75` matches numbers only.
A single aggregate answers one value.
`DESCENDANTS` matches every depth below the subject. `MAP { * }` returns whole events.
`LIMIT` is applied after loading, it is not storage pagination.
`COUNT() == n` answers a boolean. This is the shape `isQueryResultTrue` preconditions use.
GDBQL also accepts the LINQ-style spelling: `FROM e IN events ... TOP n PROJECT INTO { }`. Existing queries in that form run unchanged. New queries use `STREAM ... MAP`.
Expected to fail: not GDBQL.
API v1 route of GenesisDB 1.x.

item.name: 5 Catalog
item.description: Distinct subjects and types from the index.

request.description: First path segment of every subject, for example `/customer`, `/order`, `/user`.

item.name: 6 Subscribe (SSE)
item.description: Server-Sent Events. Postman keeps the connection open and shows events as they arrive, cancel the request to stop. Commit to the subject from a second tab to see live events.

request.description: History first, then new events in commit order. A heartbeat `data: {"payload":""}` is sent when a poll finds nothing. `interval` is seconds, 0.1 to 86400. The request runs until you cancel it.
Resume after a known event: the history starts after `lowerBound`.
API v1 route of GenesisDB 1.x.

item.name: 7 Schemas
item.description: Immutable per-type schemas. HTTP commits of the type are validated. Registering twice answers 409.

request.description: Strict JSON Schema subset: type, properties, required, additionalProperties, items, description, title. Additional fields are rejected unless `additionalProperties: true`.
NDJSON like every other list.
Expected to fail: `price` is required, `color` is not allowed.
Expected to fail: `pattern` is not part of the supported subset.
API v1 route of GenesisDB 1.x. Answers 409 because the type is registered already.

item.name: 8 Administration
item.description: Administrator token only. Backup, audit and erase hold the writer lock, commits wait meanwhile.

request.description: Verifies every event hash and predecessor link in physical log order. Text response.

Complete logical backup: events, reference data, system events and schemas. Materialized in memory, the writer lock is held meanwhile. The body is saved in the `backup` variable for Restore. Plain form is a JSON array, extended form (with references, system events or schemas) is an object.

Replaces every reference payload below the subject with `{}`, keys included. Inline `data` is immutable and not touched. Writes a requested and a completed audit system event. 404 if the subject has no events, 422 if it has events but no erasable reference data.

exec: pm.test("reports erased entries", () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.match(/^Erased \d+ ref data files/));

request.description: The event remains with its metadata and hash, `data` is now `{}`.

item.name: Erase subject with inline data only (422)

request.description: Expected to fail: inline data is immutable.
Rebuilds every index file from the event logs. Reads and writes wait meanwhile.

Restore requires a completely empty store. Against the store that produced the backup this answers 409. To test a real restore, point `baseUrl` at a fresh instance with an empty data directory and run this request there.
API v1 route of GenesisDB 1.x.

item.name: 9 Authorization
item.description: Expects rejections. The read and write token requests only work when GENESISDB_READ_TOKEN and GENESISDB_WRITE_TOKEN are configured and set in the collection variables.

request.description: Any value that is not a configured token. Resolves to two random GUIDs, Postman never sees a literal secret.
